sections.title: Right now
lines: Pregame build. Kickoff Thu 7:15 PM CT (in 21h 28m).
Sold 2,327 contracts so far. 882 more are resting on the book, on 2 of 6 sides.
By team: DEN 1,028, SEA 1,299.
Not balanced yet: the worst line is -$179; the goal is -$150 or better by kickoff, so $29 to close.
If every resting order filled, the worst line would be -$251.
Backstop (-$600) is not triggered; the loss cap is -$300.
Backing off new posts for another 3m: Kalshi refused posts for lack of free cash.
Free cash is $142 (read 2m ago). Kalshi counts resting orders against buying power, so new posts can be refused at this level.

sections.title: Lagging sides
lines: DEN by 15+: sold 200, 427 behind the leader. Cheapest row is 10c, fair 9.1c. It can step down 1c at a time, to no lower than about 6.1c (never under the crowd's clearing price or fair minus 3c), after 20 min with no fill, at most one step per 15 min. Last price step: 8h 21m ago. Next possible step now, if nothing has filled.
SEA by 7-14: sold 222, 404 behind the leader. Nothing is resting on this side right now. A catch-up batch posts when a side is lagging with nothing resting. Sold 68 here in the last hour.
DEN by 7-14: sold 307, 320 behind the leader. Nothing is resting on this side right now. A catch-up batch posts when a side is lagging with nothing resting.

SEA by 15+: sold 450, 177 behind the leader. Nothing is resting on this side right now. A catch-up batch posts when a side is lagging with nothing resting. Last hold reason (55m ago): filling one more row in full would push the worst line to -$193, so the bot holds its price.

DEN by 1-6: sold 522, 105 behind the leader. Cheapest row is 20c, fair 19.3c. It can step down 1c at a time, to no lower than about 16.3c (never under the crowd's clearing price or fair minus 3c), after 20 min with no fill, at most one step per 15 min. Last price step: 6h 45m ago. Next possible step now, if nothing has filled.

The bot looks at lagging sides every loop (1m) and takes a fresh market snapshot about every 10 min (last one 37s ago). Rows already resting are not repriced when the sportsbook line moves; only new rows use the fresh fair.
A step is skipped if filling the new row in full would push the worst line lower.

sections.title: Next wave of contracts
lines: A side gets a new batch when its resting drops under 25% of what it launched with. The batch is 50% of the launch size (a third inside T-30), split 60/25/15 at +0/+1/+2c, priced from the last hour's fills.
Closest to triggering: SEA by 7-14 with 0 resting against a trigger of 225 (launch 900). Close now.
DEN by 7-14 is thin (0 resting) but is 307 contracts ahead of the least-sold side (limit 300), so it gets no batch until the others catch up.
SEA by 1-6 is thin (0 resting) but is 627 contracts ahead of the least-sold side (limit 300), so it gets no batch until the others catch up.
SEA by 15+ is thin (0 resting) but is 450 contracts ahead of the least-sold side (limit 300), so it gets no batch until the others catch up.
The worst-line gate is open (-$179 is at or better than -$200), so a thin side would get a batch on the next loop.
Limits: up to 3 batches per side, 20 minutes apart, until T-3. Batches used so far: none.
Catch-up is due now on: DEN by 7-14, SEA by 7-14, SEA by 15+ (lagging with nothing resting).
Held back and not yet posted: DEN by 7-14: 53 contracts. The bot releases these when the batch cap and cash allow; I cannot see the exact moment.

sections.title: Tightening
lines: Trickle balancing (paid) starts at T-240: Thu 3:15 PM CT (in 17h 28m). The bot notes the worst line then, and walks it in a straight line to -$150 by T-10 (Thu 7:05 PM CT).
Rules: checks every 5 min, pays only when more than $25 behind the path, never on the most-held side, clips of up to 100 contracts, no more than $100 total paid per book. Spent so far: $0.
From T-30 (Thu 6:45 PM CT): if the worst line is -$150 or better, paid balancing stops for good; new offers keep going until kickoff.
Checkpoints (a market snapshot is logged each time): T-240, T-180, T-120, T-90, T-60, T-30.
At kickoff (Thu 7:15 PM CT) the in-game engine takes over and keeps the resting orders.

sections.title: Will it adapt on its own?
lines: Yes, on its own: lagging sides step their price down within the limits above; thin sides get new batches while the worst-line gate is open; paid balancing follows the timer.
No, it will not: reprice rows that are already resting when the sportsbook line moves, react to injury news, or cut a side that is selling fast. Check the line yourself on Wed/Thu if news breaks.

The one thing that depends on the crowd: the worst line is -$179 against a -$150 goal. Fills on the lagging sides lift it for free; if they do not come, the paid trickle covers the rest from T-240, up to $100.
I only read the bot's settings, state and log. I cannot see its next decision, only the rules it follows.

Before it gets more, that gap has to shrink to under 300, so the other sides need about 175 more fills. The next closest is SEA by 7-14, which only gets a batch once its 895 resting contracts drop below 225.
